subject: Ingress-path attestation & operational acceptance for on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Andrew Davies <andrew.davies@acme.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-engineering@acme.com, sre_lead@acme.com
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: ingress-path attestation and final acceptance checklist

Laura —

Thanks again for yesterday's bridge. We're in the final stretch for the on-prem handoff and need a short formal attestation from Redwood on a few networking and operational items so our security/compliance team can close the acceptance ticket. Can you confirm the following from your side and attach any evidence artifacts you have?

- Ingress path: firewall rules and load-balancer NAT mapping verified for control-plane and inference ports (TLS termination points noted)
- Egress posture: approved outbound destinations for telemetry + model fetch (IPs + FQDNs)
- ACLs and routing: customer-side routing table entries and Redwood’s promoted routes match the preflight plan
- KV cache priming: verification that prefix warmup completed (sample logs or token counts)
- Audit trail: links to the runbook playback recording and any post-playback run logs

We're hoping to bundle this with our security review and turn the ticket green by tomorrow if possible. If you can provide a short attestation statement and attach the key artifacts, that will expedite sign-off.

Thanks,
Andrew
Andrew Davies
Principal SRE, ACME Corp

Subject: Re: Request: ingress-path attestation and final acceptance checklist

Andrew —

Appreciate the clear checklist. We're attaching an attestation PDF and the KV priming log. Quick answers inline:

- Ingress path: confirmed. LB NAT mapping and TLS termination are running on the edge gateways we used during the dry-run (see attachment: redwood-ingress-attestation-20251106.pdf).
- Egress posture: only approved telemetry endpoints and model metadata hosts are reachable; we've included the outgoing FQDN list in the attestation PDF.
- ACLs & routing: Redwood’s promoted routes were applied at 02:00 UTC during the migration window. Customer routing table snapshot is included in the shared Drive link.
- KV cache priming: prefix warmup completed with an average hit-rate of 84% across the tested prefixes; sample log attached (kv-cache-prime-log-ACME-20251106.txt).
- Audit trail: runbook playback recording uploaded to the shared Drive (link below).

Short attestation statement (for your security team):
"Redwood Inference attests that the on-prem deployment for ACME Corp has completed ingress and egress validation, routing and ACL promotion, KV cache priming, and runbook playback. All checks completed within the agreed acceptance windows on 2025-11-06. Where temporary mitigations were used (edge NAT mapping for legacy control-plane flows), the mitigation is documented and will be remediated within the first maintenance window after cutover."

I'll follow up with any additional logs if your team needs packet captures or firewall audit trails.

Laura Bennett
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Andrew / team —

A couple of operational clarifications from the playback that might help your auditors:

- During the KB priming we observed a transient 1.2s tail latency on the model fetch path when simultaneous large prefix loads happened; this is in the priming log at 11:03 UTC. It's expected behavior under burst prime and does not affect steady-state inference latency. We've included mitigation notes in the PDF (staggered prime schedule and backoff).
- TLS cert chain: the edge gateways present the customer-managed cert chains; we recorded the cert validity window and included the fingerprint in the Drive link.
- Route analytics: we've captured BGP withdraw/reannounce events during the cutover and included them in the playback notes — nothing unexpected, but callouts are in the attachment.

If ACME wants packet captures for the 11:03 event, we can provide a sanitized pcap.

Mina Haddad
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
